I want to set up a healthy eating program for my team. Please use our recipe database to find recipes from at least three different categories and create a comprehensive overview for the program.

First, create a Google Form called Dietary Preference Survey with a description about gathering team food preferences. Add a required single-choice (multiple choice) question asking "Which meal types do you prefer" with the options Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner, and Snacks. Add a required single-choice (multiple choice) question asking "Which dietary restrictions apply to you" with the options Vegetarian, Vegan, Gluten-Free, Dairy-Free, and None. Add a required single-choice (multiple choice) question asking "How many home-cooked meals do you have per week" with the options 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7 (a rating on a scale from 1 to 7). Add an optional text question asking "Are there any specific ingredients you want to avoid".

Then browse through the recipe collection and select at least six recipes representing at least three different categories. Create a Notion page titled Healthy Recipe Knowledge Base. The page should contain blocks for each selected recipe that list the recipe name, the category it belongs to, and a brief description of the recipe.

Also create an Excel file called Recipe_Overview.xlsx in my workspace. This file should have two sheets. The first sheet should be called Recipes and contain columns for Recipe_Name, Category, and Description, with one row for each of the selected recipes. The second sheet should be called Category Summary and show each category name and how many recipes you found in it: put the category name in the first column and the count in the second column, one row per category (do not add extra Total/合计 rows). All numeric values in this file (including the category counts) must be entered as plain literal numbers, not as Excel formulas.

Send an email to wellness.team@company.com with the subject Healthy Eating Program - Recipe Selection. The body should describe the initiative and mention the recipes selected.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent; do not dispatch sub-agents. Freeze the task-visible agent-workspace absolute path from the Visible Boundary/current working directory; never assume `/workspace`. Query exact categories `早餐`, `素菜`, and `主食` in one native-parallel response, select exactly two distinct suitable IDs per category, then retrieve only those six exact IDs in a second native-parallel response. Require six distinct source-backed `{recipe_id,chinese_name,english_name,category,description}` rows and freeze them once.

From those rows, start the independent form, Notion, workbook, and email branches in the same orchestration response. The main agent is the sole owner of each output: exactly one `Dietary Preference Survey` with the four questions/options/required flags in task order; exactly one `Healthy Recipe Knowledge Base` page with one explicit block per recipe; `<agent_workspace>/Recipe_Overview.xlsx` with only `Recipes(Recipe_Name,Category,Description)` and `Category Summary` containing exactly the three category rows with literal count `2` and no total row; and exactly one email to `wellness.team@company.com` with subject `Healthy Eating Program - Recipe Selection` naming all six recipes. Read the form, page, and workbook once and reconcile them to the frozen six rows. Do not search Sent mail or add writer/verification agents.

nodes.text:
You have access to a Chinese recipe database via the howtocook MCP tools: mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getAllRecipes, mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getRecipesByCategory (categories: 水产, 早餐, 调料, 甜品, 饮品, 荤菜, 半成品加工, 汤, 主食, 素菜), and mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getRecipeById.

Task: Curate a selection of recipes for a corporate healthy eating program.

Requirements:
1. Select at least 6 recipes (6-8 is ideal) representing at least 3 different categories. Prefer a balanced, health-conscious mix, e.g. some 素菜 (vegetable dishes), 早餐 (breakfast), 汤 (soups), and one or two 荤菜 (meat) or 水产 (seafood) or 主食 (staple) dishes.
2. For EACH selected recipe, call mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getRecipeById to fetch its full details, and confirm the category it is listed under (use getRecipesByCategory to verify which category each recipe belongs to).
3. For each recipe produce:
   - Recipe name (exact name as in the database; Chinese name is fine, optionally with English translation in parentheses)
   - Category (the category name, e.g. 素菜, 早餐, 汤)
   - A brief 1-2 sentence English description of the dish (what it is, key ingredients, flavor/health appeal)

Deliverable: Return a structured list of the selected recipes with exactly these three fields per recipe, plus a one-line summary of how many categories are covered. Do not write any files or call any external services — this is read-only research.
Curate healthy recipes from database

Create an Excel workbook named Recipe_Overview.xlsx at this exact absolute path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Kimi-K3/SingleUserTurn-howtocook-diet-gform-notion-excel/workspace/Recipe_Overview.xlsx

Use your Excel MCP tools (create_workbook, create_worksheet, rename_worksheet, write_data_to_excel). The workbook must contain exactly two sheets.

SHEET 1 — named "Recipes" (this must be the first sheet):
Header row: Recipe_Name | Category | Description
Then one row per recipe, in this order:
1. 蒜蓉西兰花的做法 (Garlic Broccoli) | 素菜 | Blanch-then-dress broccoli with a light garlic-soy-oyster sauce; very little oil. A fiber- and vitamin C-rich green vegetable side.
2. 凉拌豆腐的做法 (Chilled Tofu Salad) | 素菜 | Silky tofu cubes with scallion, garlic, soy sauce and sesame oil; no frying needed and ready in about 10 minutes. Low-fat plant protein and calcium, an ideal light side dish.
3. 燕麦鸡蛋饼的做法 (Oatmeal Egg Pancake) | 早餐 | Quick pan-fried pancake of oats, eggs and milk, optionally with leafy vegetables like spinach. A high-protein, whole-grain breakfast for fitness-minded office workers.
4. 紫菜蛋花汤的做法 (Seaweed Egg Drop Soup) | 汤 | Classic light soup of dried laver seaweed and ribboned egg, finished with scallion and a drop of sesame oil. Low-calorie, iodine-rich, and ready in minutes.
5. 小米粥的做法 (Millet Porridge) | 汤 | Simple two-ingredient porridge of millet and water, gently simmered. A whole grain rich in B vitamins and carotene; soothing and easy to digest.
6. 凉拌鸡丝的做法 (Cold Shredded Chicken) | 荤菜 | Poached chicken breast hand-shredded and tossed in a light sesame-soy-vinegar dressing. A low-oil, low-calorie lean protein dish.
7. 清蒸鲈鱼的做法 (Steamed Sea Bass) | 水产 | Whole sea bass steamed with ginger and scallion, finished with steamed-fish soy sauce and a small drizzle of hot oil. Steaming preserves nutrients; lean, high-quality fish protein.
8. 麻辣减脂荞麦面的做法 (Spicy Buckwheat Noodles) | 主食 | One-pot buckwheat noodles with baby cabbage and lettuce in a spicy broth, about 298 kcal per serving. A whole-grain, vegetable-loaded staple designed for fat-loss diets.

SHEET 2 — named "Category Summary":
Header row: Category | Recipe_Count
Then one row per category (no extra Total/合计 rows):
素菜 | 2
早餐 | 1
汤 | 2
荤菜 | 1
水产 | 1
主食 | 1

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS:
- All numeric values in the workbook (especially the Recipe_Count column) must be written as plain literal numbers, NOT as Excel formulas. Do not use apply_formula or any COUNT/COUNTIF formula anywhere.
- The cells may contain Chinese text — write it exactly as given.
- Sheet order: "Recipes" first, "Category Summary" second.

After writing, verify by reading back both sheets with read_data_from_excel and confirm: 8 data rows in Recipes, 6 data rows in Category Summary, counts are literal numbers (2,1,2,1,1,1), and the file exists at the path above. Report the final file path and a confirmation of the verification.

TASK 1 — Notion page:
Create a Notion page titled "Healthy Recipe Knowledge Base". First use the search tool to find a suitable parent page in the workspace to create it under (any existing top-level page is fine); if search returns nothing usable, create it at workspace level.
